chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked:
About the man who enters the bathhouse while he is fasting, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, as long as he does not fear weakness.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a fasting person to enter a bathhouse?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that entering the bathhouse while fasting is permissible (ja'iz) based on the principle of removing hardship, provided the individual does not fear that the heat or exertion will cause significant weakness (da'f) that could invalidate the fast. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on 'la haraj' (no difficulty), distinguishing between mere discomfort and actual impairment of the fast's spiritual and physical integrity. The condition of fearing weakness highlights the subjective nature of the ruling, allowing for personal assessment of one's capacity to maintain the fast during the day.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
having been asked about the man who enters the bathhouse and he is Fasting. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem for as long as he does not fear weakness’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who uses the bathhouse when fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful as long as he is not afraid of becoming weak.’”
